name: sc68
desc: Play music originally designed for Atari ST and Amiga computers
why: Plays original Atari ST and Amiga music formats, letting you hear old chiptune sound-engine files directly.

brief.what_it_is: sc68 is a free, open source project that plays music originally made for Atari ST and Amiga computers. It is distributed as an input plugin for common music players such as Winamp and XMMS, and the project also ships a large collection of Atari ST and Amiga soundchip tunes. The archive holds only music that needs unusual or custom players, not standard Amiga .mod files. The executables from Homebrew (as68, debug68, info68, sc68, sc68-config, sourcer68, unice68) are not described on the pages I read.
brief.why_it_exists: The project intends to play musics originally designed for Atari ST and Amiga computers. Its archive keeps tunes that need custom players, which general music players do not support.
brief.install_notes: The homepage points to a download section, and that page links to SourceForge for the latest releases. Version 2.2.1 has a Win32 installer that includes a Winamp-3 component, and a Winamp-2 plugin is still maintained. Older releases are offered as source packages (1.2.1, 1.2.0, 1.0.1, 1.0.0) and a Windows installer for 1.2.x. No commands, accounts, or runtime setup were shown in the pages I read.
brief.standout: It is a player for chiptune formats that most players cannot open, and it is paired with a curated archive of tunes that need those custom players. It was also ported to the Dreamcast as part of the dcplaya project.
brief.status: Quiet, as far as I can tell. The latest release listed is 2.2.1, but the pages show no release dates and no recent commit information. The site footer reads 'sc68 website ©sashipa Nov 2003' and 'Design by Benjamin Gerard', which suggests the site has not changed in a long time. I did not check SourceForge, so this is uncertain.
brief.caveats: The homepage is thin and gives no commands, usage examples, or formats list. The developers page I guessed at returned HTTP 404, so the 'Technical features' and developer details were not read. Some download links were not given as URLs in the text, so I did not follow them. The Homebrew description calls it music for Atari ST and Amiga computers, which matches the project. The brew caveats field is empty. The Winamp and XMMS plugins are the main way to play, and the homepage does not describe a standalone CLI.

entry.title: sc68
entry.tldr: A player for Atari ST and Amiga soundchip music that ordinary players cannot open, with a command-line tool and a few extras installed by Homebrew.
entry.deeper_look:
sc68 plays music originally written for Atari ST and Amiga computers. In the project's words, it "intends to play musics originally designed for Atari ST and Amiga computers." Much of this music is not a recording or a simple module file. It needs custom players, which is why general music players skip it.

The project also keeps an archive of tunes that need those players. It leaves out standard Amiga .mod files: "Do not expect to find any Amigatm modules [.mod] music file, since this file format is already supported by most music player softwares." The scope is the odd material that nothing else handles.

The idea underneath is preservation through emulation. Old machines made sound with specific chips and with code written for those chips, and playing that music faithfully means reproducing how the hardware behaved. That is a way into chiptune history and into how sound engines worked on 1980s and 1990s home computers.

Homebrew installs seven executables: as68, debug68, info68, sc68, sc68-config, sourcer68 and unice68. The pages read for this entry do not describe them. The names suggest an assembler, a debugger, an info tool, a source tool and an unpacker, but that is a guess from the names. The project documents its Winamp and XMMS plugins as the main way to play. It was also ported to the Dreamcast as part of the dcplaya project.
entry.install:
brew install sc68

You will also need some sc68-format music files. The project's archive is the place to look, starting from the homepage.

entry.whats_unique: It opens Atari ST and Amiga music formats that most players cannot, and it comes with an archive of tunes that need those custom players. The Homebrew package also ships a set of developer-style tools alongside the player.
entry.caveats: The site looks untouched since about 2003, the homepage gives no usage examples, and the docs I read do not describe the command-line tools, so expect to learn them from --help.
